title: Open-source guard frameworks
summary: NeMo Guardrails orchestrates rails around an LLM, Guardrails AI runs validators on inputs and outputs, and Llama Guard is a safety classifier model. You self-host them when data location, taxonomy or language rule out the managed service.
useIf: Data cannot leave your environment, your policy taxonomy is custom, or you need flow control and validation logic the platform guardrails do not offer.
avoidIf: A managed guardrail already meets the need: self-hosting adds GPUs, evaluation work and upgrade churn.

explain.md: **NeMo Guardrails** is an open-source Python library, also deployable as a Kubernetes microservice with the same YAML and Colang configuration. It names five rail types: input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output. Built-ins cover content safety, jailbreak detection, topic control, PII handling and fact-checking, with integrations for Llama Guard, NemoGuard models and third-party APIs. Its `self check facts` output rail uses `$relevant_chunks` as evidence and returns a 0.0 to 1.0 score that depends on the LLM following the prompt. If a reasoning model spends its `max_tokens` budget before answering, the rail fails closed (score 0.0, response blocked) [[r13]] [[r14]]. The docs list releases v0.22.0 to v0.24.1 plus a Latest build, so pin a version.

**Guardrails AI** is a Python framework that runs Input and Output Guards built from validators in Guardrails Hub, and also produces structured output. The Hub showed 65 validators on 2026-10-13 (for example ban list, toxic language, detect jailbreak and detect PII, which uses Microsoft Presidio), and that count changes often [[r15]] [[r29]] [[r17]].

**Llama Guard** is a safety classifier model. Llama Guard 4 has 12B parameters, is natively multimodal (early fusion), runs on one GPU and is a drop-in for Llama Guard 3 8B and 11B. Llama Guard 3 1B remains useful at the edge. It classifies prompt text and an image together, not an image alone. Llama Guard 3 uses categories S1 Violent Crimes to S14 Code Interpreter Abuse, and the category text in the prompt can be rewritten, which is how you encode a custom taxonomy [[r16]].

explain.title: Self-hosting does not remove evaluation
explain.md: Whichever framework you pick, you own the labelled test set, the thresholds and the upgrade regression runs.

whereToUse: On-premises or sovereign deployments where prompts cannot go to a managed API
Products with a custom safety taxonomy (for example domain-specific advice rules)
Dialog systems that need scripted flows and topic control, not only classification
Python services that need schema validation plus lightweight content checks
Edge or latency-sensitive paths using a small classifier model

use: Use Llama Guard when you need a self-hosted classifier with rewritable categories
Use NeMo Guardrails when you need rails across input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output
Use Guardrails AI when validators and structured output are the main need
Combine them with deterministic checks for exact rules
avoid: Avoid self-hosting when you cannot run GPUs or maintain an evaluation set
Avoid unpinned framework versions: behaviour changes between releases
Avoid relying on an LLM-prompt rail with a reasoning model without testing the `max_tokens` budget
flips: Data may go to a managed API and categories are standard: use platform guardrails
Image-only moderation is needed: Llama Guard 4 classifies text and image together, so add another image classifier
Policy is mostly exact rules: deterministic checks beat a classifier on cost and clarity

pitfalls.symptom: The fact-checking rail blocks every answer after a model change
pitfalls.cause: A reasoning model used its whole `max_tokens` budget before answering, so the rail failed closed with a 0.0 score
pitfalls.fix: Raise the budget or use a non-reasoning model for the rail

pitfalls.symptom: Behaviour changes after a library upgrade
pitfalls.cause: Framework releases change defaults and prompts (NeMo docs list several releases)
pitfalls.fix: Pin versions and rerun the evaluation set on every upgrade

pitfalls.symptom: A rewritten Llama Guard category over-flags or misses
pitfalls.cause: Category text changed the classifier's behaviour without recalibration
pitfalls.fix: Evaluate the new taxonomy on labelled data before use

pitfalls.symptom: A Hub validator passes demos but fails on real data
pitfalls.cause: Validator quality and coverage vary by language and domain
pitfalls.fix: Treat validators as components and test them on your own set

scenarios.title: On-premises assistant with a custom policy
scenarios.situation: A regulated firm runs an assistant on its own infrastructure. Prompts and documents cannot be sent to an external API. Policy forbids personal investment recommendations, which standard harm categories do not cover.
constraints: A labelled policy test set can be built
unknowns: What latency can the guard add?
scenarios.question: Which guard approach fits?

options.name: Self-hosted Llama Guard with rewritten category text, plus deterministic checks for exact rules
options.why: It runs in house and the category text can encode the custom policy.
options.tradeoff: GPU operation and the work to calibrate the new category.

options.name: NeMo Guardrails with Colang flows calling a local model
options.why: Strong flow and topic control without external calls.
options.tradeoff: Heavier configuration and an LLM call per rail.

options.name: A managed content safety API
options.why: Data leaves the environment and the policy is not a standard category.
options.tradeoff: Right when data may be sent and categories are standard.

flips.if: Data may go to a compliant managed service
flips.then: Use platform guardrails plus a custom classifier for the policy.

flips.if: The policy is a short list of phrases

scenarios.takeaway: Data location and custom taxonomy are the usual reasons to self-host.

scenarios.title: Python service that must return valid JSON
scenarios.situation: A small team runs a Python service that must return schema-valid JSON and block a ban list of terms plus basic PII. They want results this month with little infrastructure.
scenarios.question: Which framework do you start with?

options.name: Guardrails AI with Hub validators for structured output, ban list and PII
options.why: It is a Python library built around input and output guards and structured output, with no GPU needed.
options.tradeoff: Validator quality varies, so you test on your data.

options.name: NeMo Guardrails
options.why: Covers more rail types than this job needs and runs in Python.
options.tradeoff: More configuration than this need requires.

options.name: Train a custom classifier first
options.why: It delays delivery and needs labelled data and GPUs.
options.tradeoff: Right once off-the-shelf validators clearly fail on your data.

flips.if: The product adds multi-turn flows with strict topics
flips.then: Move to NeMo Guardrails for dialog rails.
Add Llama Guard behind a guard.

scenarios.takeaway: Start with the lightest tool that meets the requirement.

quiz.q: Which statement about Llama Guard 4 is correct?
options: It has 12B parameters, is natively multimodal and runs on one GPU
It classifies an image alone without text
It only works for English text
It is a managed Azure service
quiz.explain: Llama Guard 4 is a 12B natively multimodal open-weights model that runs on one GPU. It classifies text and image together, not an image alone, and it is not an Azure service.

quiz.q: Which are NeMo Guardrails rail types?
quiz.explain: NeMo names input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output rails. Compression is not a rail type.

quiz.q: Your NeMo `self check facts` rail suddenly blocks all answers after you switch to a reasoning model. Most likely cause?
options: The model spent its whole `max_tokens` budget thinking, so the rail scored 0.0 and failed closed
quiz.explain: The documentation notes the rail fails closed with a 0.0 score when a reasoning model uses its `max_tokens` before answering. The other causes do not match the symptom.

flashcards.back: Input, retrieval, dialog, execution and output. Retrieval rails filter chunks, execution rails check tool calls.
A Python framework running Input and Output Guards from Hub validators (65 on 2026-10-13), also producing structured output.

flashcards.front: How do you encode a custom policy in Llama Guard?
flashcards.back: Rewrite the category text in the prompt, then evaluate on labelled data. It classifies text and image together, not an image alone.
